records.headline: Could a shipwreck exist when the ship is gone?
records.discoverSummary: An archaeological find off Türkiye may point to a shipwreck from as early as 2700 BCE, yet no ship hull survived. The mystery raises a fascinating question: how can researchers identify a wreck from what remains around it?

records.headline: The Rosetta Stone's long road to decipherment
records.discoverSummary: A stone found in 1799 carried the same decree in three scripts, but translating its Egyptian hieroglyphs took decades and competing scholars. The story shows how a chance discovery became a key to understanding an ancient civilization.

records.headline: The triple-star system astronomers weren't searching for
records.discoverSummary: Astronomers seeking planets near a red dwarf instead uncovered a rare system with two white dwarfs just 28 light-years away. Its unlikely configuration is challenging ideas about how closely orbiting stars survive one another's evolution.

records.headline: A hidden giant planet emerges from old telescope images
records.discoverSummary: A new technique for reducing starlight glare revealed a giant exoplanet in existing James Webb Space Telescope data. The finding illustrates how better analysis can unlock discoveries from observations scientists already possess.

records.headline: A 42-year search finds evidence of an extraordinarily rare decay
records.discoverSummary: Researchers studying collisions at the LHC found initial evidence for a rare particle decay long predicted by physics. The result is promising but has not reached the stronger statistical standard physicists use to claim a discovery.

records.headline: Four individual gold medals make Youth Olympic history
records.discoverSummary: Japanese swimmer Mana Ishikawa won four individual gold medals at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games, a first in the event's history. Her run of victories offers a compelling young-athlete milestone beyond the usual professional sports headlines.

records.headline: Wushu makes a medal-winning Youth Olympic debut
records.discoverSummary: Wushu awarded its first Youth Olympic medals at Dakar 2026, expanding the spotlight on a martial art previously featured in Olympic settings as an exhibition event. Four golds marked the competition's debut.

records.headline: A Statue of Liberty portrait in under a minute
records.discoverSummary: A speed painter created a Statue of Liberty portrait in less than 60 seconds as part of Guinness World Records Day. It's an entertaining demonstration of skill that makes for a quick, surprising discovery.

records.headline: A giant squash mosaic honors a natural-history storyteller
records.discoverSummary: A farm assembled a huge portrait of David Attenborough and a frog from thousands of pumpkins and squashes. The playful display combines community creativity, seasonal harvests and an unexpected form of art.

records.headline: A reading event brings thousands together across countries
records.discoverSummary: A record-setting online reading campaign brought together more than 153,000 participants across 92 countries. The collaborative achievement offers a feel-good discovery about how shared curiosity and a few minutes with a book can unite people.
